title: Petra and the Debt
premise: Ulyana Vane, a fixer-interpreter who cleans up the failures of doomed peace processes, discovers the off-books safe house he's lived in for years has been listed online — every room photographed, including the wall of files he was never supposed to keep. The listing is a message from someone inside the delegation's security detail, offering to sell him out unless he helps them stage an 'accident' at the summit that will kill the peace deal and bury their debts with it. Ulyana must trace the leak through the city's gray market of brokers and ex-militia while deciding whether justice means exposing the plot through official channels — which would destroy him too — or handling it himself. In the end, he lets the summit proceed, delivers the conspirators to no one, and finally signs his own name to something: the deed of the safe house, bought at auction, no longer invisible.
about_author: Dominic Reyes is the pen name of a former NGO field coordinator who spent a decade in ceasefire corridors before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about people whose jobs exist only in the margins of official history.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Ulyana Vane, POV. Scrolling property sites at 2 a.m., Ulyana finds the safe house listed with interior photos — including his file wall. He recognizes the camera angle as one only someone with access could take. The emotional beat is cold dread: years of careful invisibility collapsing in a single webpage.

chapters.title: Interpreter's Privilege
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. He works a pre-summit mediation session, translating threats dressed as courtesies, while cataloguing who had safe house access. A junior security officer, Mara Ilves, watches him too closely. Beat: professional composure stretched over rising paranoia; he realizes the attack may already be scheduled around the summit calendar.

chapters.title: Who Owns Nothing
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. He visits the gray-market broker who arranged the safe house lease and learns the property's ownership chain was scrubbed three weeks ago — by someone with delegation credentials. Beat: the vertigo of learning his sanctuary was never really his, and that his erasure was someone else's project first.

chapters.title: Mara
chapters.summary: Mara Ilves, POV. She tails Ulyana through the old quarter, torn between loyalty to her unit and the evidence she's found in its expense ledgers. She confronts him obliquely at a café. Beat: two hunters discovering they're both prey; wary alliance formed over shared suspicion of their own side.

chapters.title: The Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Following money trails through ex-militia contacts, he uncovers the scheme: war-crimes payouts owed to victims were diverted into the delegates' private accounts, and the summit 'accident' will kill the witnesses scheduled to testify. Beat: moral fury — this isn't just self-preservation, it's justice outside any courtroom that would ever convene.

chapters.title: Accident Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Alternating Ulyana and Mara POVs. They infiltrate the venue's maintenance contractor and find the gas-line modification already installed, timed for the opening plenary. They photograph it, but the photos vanish from Mara's phone within hours. Beat: escalating dread — the conspiracy is inside their communications, watching them back.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. The conspirator behind the listing — deputy security chief Aldous Renk — summons him and offers immunity and a new identity if he stays silent, revealing he knows about Ulyana's own buried case files. Beat: temptation and shame; Ulyana sees his whole career of deniable work reflected in Renk's corruption.

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. With the summit imminent, Mara goes to the delegation head and is disbelieved, then suspended. She and Ulyana plan outside the law entirely: reroute the venue inspection, bait Renk with a fake witness list. Beat: resolve hardening into action; belonging found not in institutions but in one trustworthy ally.

chapters.title: The Plenary
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Summit day. The bait works — Renk's team moves to trigger the 'accident' early and is caught on record by the inspectors Ulyana redirected. Renk, cornered, takes Ulyana hostage in the service tunnels. Beat: climax; Ulyana talks him down not with force but by translating, aloud, exactly what Renk's death would mean to the people waiting outside.

chapters.title: Deed of Sale
chapters.summary: Ulyana, POV. Weeks later: Renk and his network face quiet tribunals, the victims' fund partially restored, and Ulyana's own files sealed by a judge who owes him nothing and gives everything. At auction, he buys the safe house under his real name. Beat: resolution — inheritance claimed at last; invisibility exchanged, deliberately, for belonging.
